title: Donation slice rounds down via integer division `(sUSDSAmount * batchDonationSize) / 100`; for small sUSDSAmount values the donation is effectively skipped and the entire balance flows to LP
description: `uint256 donationSUSDS = (sUSDSAmount * batchDonationSize) / 100;` followed by `donationActive = donationSUSDS > 0 && ...`. For small sUSDSAmount (e.g., 99 wei with batchDonationSize = 1, gives donationSUSDS = 0) the donation is skipped and all sUSDS flows to addLiquidity. This is dust-edge behaviour rather than an exploit per se — but in combination with the BalancerPoolerMintDebtHook, the hook still accrues phUSD debt based on the USDS notional received in `_dispatch`, regardless of whether the eventual pool() call routes any USDC through the donation path. Tiny dispatches therefore accrue debt with NO matching USDC output. This is a contributor to ECON-RAW-003 Scenario B and is called out separately because the rounding-down is the on-chain mechanism by which the hook<->dispatcher invariant first diverges for small flows.
exploit_path: Not directly an exploit. Tracked as a low because: (a) it documents the precise rounding direction of the donation slice (down, favouring the LP side, away from batchMinter); (b) cumulative small dispatches drift the hook's mintDebt above what the donation path will ever realise.
mainnet_realism: Sub-wei rounding. Mainnet-realistic but with negligible per-call impact.
recommendation: If the protocol-level invariant requires donation parity, either accumulate the dust into a separate counter and trigger when it crosses a threshold, or use higher precision (e.g., multiply batchDonationSize by 1e18/100 once and divide by 1e18) — but realistically the cleanest fix is the ECON-RAW-003 recommendation (accrue mintDebt from realised USDC, not dispatched USDS).
severity_rationale: Confirmed Low/QA. Sub-wei rounding-down on the donation slice. Negligible per-call impact (dust amounts). Documented separately because the rounding direction (favouring LP side, away from batchMinter) is the on-chain mechanism by which the hook<->dispatcher invariant first diverges for small flows. Per C4 QA: dust amounts / rounding errors are QA at best. Fits Low.
